title: All things in common (Acts 2:37–47)
hookLine: teaching, fellowship, bread, prayer, and daily added
tomorrow: a man begs at the temple gate. Peter has no money. now what?

cards: The group chat after a great retreat usually goes quiet within a week. Acts says this crowd didn't. When Peter finishes, "they were pricked in their heart," and they ask, "Men and brethren, what shall we do?"
He tells them to repent and be baptized, and Acts counts about three thousand added that day. Then the real question: did it last?
Here's what they actually did: "they continued stedfastly in the apostles' doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers."

teach.b: Four things: teaching, fellowship, bread, prayer. Some readers hear the breaking of bread as the Lord's Supper, others as shared meals, some as both.
Then the line behind today's title: "And all that believed were together, and had all things common." They sold what they owned "and parted them to all men, as every man had need."

teach.h: HOUSE TO HOUSE, AT THE TABLE.
teach.b: The last picture is a kitchen table: "breaking bread from house to house, did eat their meat with gladness and singleness of heart." Meat, in the King James, simply means food.
Readers take this page different ways: a pattern to copy, a challenge, a portrait of one bright season. Acts just tells it.
One to tell a friend tonight: the Greek word for fellowship here is koinonia, from the same family as the word for common. Sharing a life and sharing a table are one idea. And notice the mood word.
Gladness, around food, in ordinary houses.

how: Some churches share a meal after worship, and some read Acts 2:42–47 as a picture of what a congregation can be.

games.q: what does “all things in common” mean?
o: owning nothing at all, by strict rule
sharing what you have, as each one needs
splitting everything in exactly equal parts

games.q: the first community — tap the pairs.
p: the crowd, pricked in their heart

s: Acts says everyone received exactly equal shares
they parted them to all men, as every man had need.
'meat' in the King James here simply means food
did eat their meat with gladness: their food, shared house to house.

games.q: you share a fridge with roommates. one buys most of the groceries; another is broke this month. what does Acts 2 point toward?
o: share by need this month, without keeping score.
split every bill exactly equal, every time.
each keeps their own shelf, so it stays fair.
games.why: Acts says they parted things to all men, as every man had need. not equal shares: need, and with gladness.

practice: Take one slow sip or bite of whatever is near: water, tea, a piece of bread. Taste it all the way through, as if it were shared.
Then bring to mind who you'd most like at your table this week, and whose table you'd be glad to sit at.

wordCard.voice: All things in common. The believers in Acts 2 shared what they had, as anyone had need, and ate together with gladness.

orig.note: Greek: fellowship, sharing. Acts 2:42; the same word family as koina, common, in 2:44.

carryVoice: Carry this: with gladness, around ordinary tables, sharing as anyone has need. Another week, done.
